recap.text: Read the club's flyer; Muse Ember; 2.7 seconds
recap.source: One capture pass by the deck builder on 2026-11-13 between 4:09 and 4:25 AM PT, against a local production build of main with the Muse key linked and the server clock set to the demo clock (3:05 PM ET; motion/opening/tools/demo-clock.cjs, driven by capture-pass.sh). Each run loads the real screen in a 390 x 797 frame, the app area the stage's phone gives an app below its status bar, as the right person, and reads the app's own time stamp (motion/opening/tools/recap-pass.mjs; every run in motion/opening/recap-pass.json). Steps the app answers once per server (re-plan, picks, hello) ran on a fresh server per run, so every stamp is a first, real call. The deck shows the median run's screen and that run's own number, so they cannot disagree. appendix.text: 197 commits on main; 131 pull requests merged; 64 test files; 1221 updates on the shared board; five people
appendix.source: Counted 2026-11-13 04:17 PST. In the product repo: git fetch origin; git rev-list --count origin/main (197); gh pr list --repo aaron-sulbaran/meta-MIUT --state merged --limit 500 --json number, counted the entries (131); git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/main | grep -c '\.test\.ts$' (64). Hub events: the hub stores one JSON file per action under events/<date>/, so find events -type f -name '*.json' | wc -l (1221). People: five, from the hub's team list.

appendix.text: Why not just build this on Instagram? The events live on Facebook: found there, RSVPs there. Instagram is one way in, like a flyer photo or a spoken line. The goal is more young adults opening Facebook, so the product has to live there.
appendix.source: The team's own position, from the hub (kb/pitch-qa.md, kb/product-brief.md, kb/idea-review.md, kb/hacktx-meta-feedback.md, mentor notes).

appendix.text: Why would young adults use this? People our age open Facebook to get something out of it. Free food is the Events version of that. It changes daily: three picks for today, and an alert only when something free is close and you are free.
appendix.source: The team's own position, from the hub (kb/pitch-qa.md, kb/product-brief.md, kb/idea-review.md, kb/hacktx-meta-feedback.md, mentor notes).

appendix.text: Is the AI essential or decorative? Essential. Six moments in the skit were live calls to Meta's Muse models, each timed on screen. Without them nobody types events in, so there is nothing to show.
appendix.source: The team's own position, from the hub (kb/pitch-qa.md, kb/product-brief.md, kb/idea-review.md, kb/hacktx-meta-feedback.md, mentor notes). Times come from recap/proof.js, the same capture pass as the recap.

appendix.text: What is real and what is staged in the demo? Every Muse answer is a live call, and a recorded one says so on screen. The Instagram, Reels and lock screen moments are staged, and so is the friend graph. We say which is which.
appendix.source: The team's own position, from the hub (kb/pitch-qa.md, kb/product-brief.md, kb/idea-review.md, kb/hacktx-meta-feedback.md, mentor notes).

appendix.text: How does it get events without extra work for organizers? An organizer shares a flyer photo or says one line. Muse drafts the event, shows where each field came from, and the organizer only approves. An Instagram post can feed the same draft.
appendix.source: The team's own position, from the hub (kb/pitch-qa.md, kb/product-brief.md, kb/idea-review.md, kb/hacktx-meta-feedback.md, mentor notes).

appendix.text: What about privacy, location and company? Both are off by default. Lisa turned on Open to company herself, and only then could Muse suggest her to someone new. Location stays opt in too. We plan per-person controls, not one rule for everyone.

appendix.text: What would it take inside Facebook? Events already cross-posts from Instagram, so this extends it. It needs Muse reading the post, the Events tab ranking per student, and a nearby alert. We built each piece on the Muse API.
